name: ariestools-skills
description: Agent skills for Aries Tools TypeScript development: shared conventions, the @ariestools/toolchain xy CLI, ESLint and TypeScript configs, Vitest presets, dependency policy, the @ariestools/sdk utility libraries, the @ariestools/sdk-react React UI libraries, actor-kit actors and providers with their cli-kit and browser-kit hosts, repository documentation conventions for agents (AGENTS.md, docs/papers lifecycle, xy agent lint), product planning from idea to MVP (papers, roadmap, per-version PRDs), and distributed architecture with autonomous replaceable workers, protocol-defined authority, reconciliation, safe concurrency and justified coordination.
shortDescription: Aries Tools development, toolchain, SDK, React, actor-kit, agent documentation, product planning, and distributed architecture skills.
longDescription: A layered skill stack for Aries Tools repositories: TypeScript/Git/testing standards (xy-development), the @ariestools/* toolchain surface — xy CLI, configs, vitest-config, deplint (xy-toolchain) — and three sibling library skills on top: the @ariestools/sdk utility libraries plus specialist packages (ariestools-sdk), the @ariestools/sdk-react React UI packages with their peers, import rule and house patterns (ariestools-sdk-react), and actor-kit actors, providers and the actor engine with the cli-kit and browser-kit hosts (ariestools-actor). Three cross-cutting companions sit beside the stack. Repository documentation conventions cover the AGENTS.md entry point, per-tool adapters, the docs/ and papers/ lifecycle, and xy agent lint (xy-agent). Product planning turns an idea into a plan of record: White, Yellow and Green papers with optional Red and Light papers, version pins between them, a roadmap with an MVP line, and one PRD per major version (xy-product-plan). The tool-independent architecture skill establishes a preference for autonomous replaceable workers governed by explicit protocols, independent work discovery, durable evidence and reconciliation, safe concurrency and normal recovery. It requires scoped coordination to be justified by a named invariant or resource constraint and distinguishes local lifecycle supervision from application-level authority (ariestools-architecture).
defaultPrompts: Use @ariestools/sdk fetchJson with a custom fetcher
Fix xy agent lint findings in this repo's AGENTS.md and docs/
Fix xy deplint findings for a private service
Write a PeriodicActor and run it in a CLI with @ariestools/cli-kit
Turn this product idea into White, Yellow and Green papers and an MVP roadmap
Design autonomous replaceable workers with protocol-defined authority and review every coordination requirement
